newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU SOURCES SEE POSSIBLE WHEAT EXPORT TAX CUT.
newsitem.headline: EU SOURCES SEE POSSIBLE WHEAT EXPORT TAX CUT.

text.p: An easing of the dollar and U.S. wheat prices, if maintained, could allow a slight reduction in European Union wheat export taxes on Thursday, European Commission sources said.

The sources stressed that last week's hike in export taxes, including a doubling of the soft wheat grain export tax to six Ecus a tonne, was aimed at calming the market and ensuring adequate supplies at reasonable prices for domestic consumers.
"The aim is to control the flow, not to block exports," said one source, noting that traders were still seeking licences to export durum wheat flour and semolina despite taxes of 22.50 Ecus a tonne.
The source said that bids last week for over one million tonnes of wheat exports were speculative and "over the top".
The priority is to supply the domestic market, added the source, noting that some 170 million tonnes out of total EU grain production of around 200 million tonnes was consumed locally in 1996/97.
